title: The NSIS installer contains only the shell executable and cannot locate its backend application tree
observed_behavior: The active NSIS bundle configuration declares an icon and target but no resources. The installed shell refuses to start unless it finds an external apps/desktop-style root containing webview/static/index.html. Read-only 7-Zip inspection of the existing 2026.6.4+001 NSIS artifact showed only NSIS plug-ins and mediapipeline-tauri-shell.exe; it contained no webview, Python runtime, src, ops, backend, or resource tree.
expected_invariant: A promoted installer must contain every immutable runtime asset needed to resolve the desktop root, start the bundled Python backend, serve the operational WebView, and execute supported backend flows on a clean machine without a source checkout.
root_cause: The Tauri bundle has no resources mapping, while runtime path resolution still assumes a repository/portable-bundle directory layout external to the executable. Productization config generation changes signing/updater fields but does not add resources.
failure_scenario: A beta user installs the signed NSIS package and launches it from the Start menu. resolve_desktop_root checks parent and apps/desktop candidates, finds no webview/static/index.html, and setup terminates before the backend or main window opens.
evidence: tauri.conf.json lines 18-40 has no bundle.resources entry.
dialogs.rs lines 58-98 makes the external WebView tree a hard startup requirement.
7-Zip list-only inspection of MediaPipelineRemuxEncodeAIO_2026.6.4+001_x64-setup.exe listed only six NSIS support files and mediapipeline-tauri-shell.exe.
New-TauriProductizationConfig.ps1 changes bundle target/updater/signing metadata but contains no resources mapping.
The scoped productization tests passed, demonstrating that they validate wiring/metadata rather than the real installer payload's startup completeness.
existing_safeguards: Tauri build produces an NSIS artifact.
CI verifies Authenticode and updater sidecars.
resolve_desktop_root fails closed instead of guessing an invalid root.
safeguard_gap: Artifact existence, signature, and metadata tests do not enumerate the real installer payload or launch an installed copy, so a correctly signed but nonfunctional installer passes.
tests_present: private-beta preflight, installed-layout, and release-artifact tests
Tauri scaffold and Rust path-candidate tests
tests_missing: real NSIS payload inventory assertion for all required runtime roots
fresh-user install-and-open validation from the installed directory
backend/WebView startup proof with no repository checkout on PATH
recommended_remediation: Define explicit immutable Tauri resources for the WebView, bundled Python/runtime, Python package source, ops scripts, schemas, and required tools using an installed layout that resolve_desktop_root understands. Make CI extract or install the exact NSIS artifact, verify the resource manifest and hashes, then open/close it on a clean Windows account.
remediation_risk: high: packaging the wrong mutable/runtime directories could expose personal state, duplicate authorities, or make updates overwrite operator data; preserve the AppData/runtime separation and release exclusions
validation_rung: Rung 5 package build, read-only payload inventory, clean-account install/open/close, backend contract/WebView startup, installed-layout verification, signature/updater verification, and package rollback; no real media is required for startup proof
prior_audit_relationship: New executable-package completeness defect proven against current config and the existing installer artifact; current docs claim package-mode promotion but did not reconcile payload contents.

title: Backend ownership does not survive shell crashes or failed startup cleanup
observed_behavior: The backend is owned only by an in-process Rust Child and best-effort shutdown/Drop logic. A shell crash never runs Drop. During startup failures, terminate_child logs a failed taskkill verification and then the function returns, dropping the last Child handle even though the process tree may still be alive. The lifecycle boundary explicitly documents that the Python backend continues after a Tauri crash.
expected_invariant: The native shell/backend lifecycle must have an OS-enforced or durably recoverable ownership model that cannot silently leave an unowned backend or worker tree after abnormal shell termination or failed cleanup verification.
root_cause: There is no Windows Job Object with kill-on-owner-close, guardian process, durable reattachment identity, or startup reconciliation of an already-running shell-owned backend. The single-instance mutex protects only while the shell process remains alive.
failure_scenario: The shell crashes during active work, or startup validation fails while taskkill cannot verify termination. The mutex disappears but the old backend remains. A new shell starts a second backend, while the original can retain locks, continue workers, mutate journals/state, or serve a still-valid bearer token without any owning UI.
evidence: BackendProcess::drop is process-local and cannot run after hard termination.
Every startup error after spawn calls terminate_child, which swallows verification failure and returns the startup error.
terminate_process_tree delegates to taskkill /T /F and has no retained ownership after its error is logged.
TAURI_BACKEND_LIFECYCLE_BOUNDARY.md lines 94-97 states that the backend continues if the Tauri shell crashes.
Rust tests cover graceful/forced shutdown and retained ownership within a live process, not hard shell death or start_backend cleanup failure.
existing_safeguards: per-user shell mutex
backend close-readiness and graceful shutdown route
grace-period taskkill tree fallback
in-process retained ownership when shutdown verification fails
safeguard_gap: All safeguards require the shell process to remain alive; none binds child lifetime or makes the orphan discoverable/reattachable after shell death.
tests_present: 56 Rust unit tests including shutdown resolution and lifecycle polling
tests_missing: hard-kill shell test proving backend/descendants are either terminated or safely reattached
taskkill failure during each startup validation branch
second launch after shell crash with an extant old backend
active-work crash/recovery evidence with unchanged media/source hashes
recommended_remediation: Adopt an explicit Windows lifecycle design: either assign the backend tree to a securely configured Job Object with kill-on-job-close where that is safe, or use a durable guardian/lease and authenticated reattachment protocol that prevents a second backend and retains close-readiness authority. Keep verified ownership on startup cleanup failure and expose actionable recovery rather than dropping the handle.
remediation_risk: high: unconditional kill-on-close could interrupt active media work, while reattachment can accidentally trust an unrelated process; design and validate process identity, token rotation, locks, descendants, and crash recovery together
validation_rung: Rung 5 package/open/close plus Windows fault injection for shell hard kill, startup-gate failure, taskkill failure, descendant processes, restart, and active-work recovery; representative real-media validation is required before changing active-work termination policy
prior_audit_relationship: Current documentation acknowledges abnormal-exit continuation but treats stale ActiveJobs reconciliation as sufficient; this review identifies the still-live unowned process and duplicate-backend gap.

title: Productized startup can execute ambient Python and import inherited PYTHONPATH code
observed_behavior: resolve_python always accepts the literal command python after bundled candidates, without checking its resolved path or restricting the fallback to debug builds. start_backend also appends the inherited PYTHONPATH to the application src root and launches without isolated/safe-path or no-user-site controls.
expected_invariant: A productized desktop application must execute a verified bundled Python runtime and import only release-owned modules; developer PATH and PYTHONPATH fallbacks must not cross into release startup.
root_cause: Development convenience fallback and inherited interpreter environment are shared unchanged by debug and release builds. MEDIAPIPELINE_PRODUCTIZED_APP labels the child after selection but does not harden interpreter provenance or import search paths.
failure_scenario: A machine lacks the expected bundled interpreter, or an earlier writable directory is present in PATH/PYTHONPATH or user site-packages. Launch runs an unrelated python.exe or imports a shadow mediapipeline package/module, executing attacker- or user-controlled code with the app's filesystem and media permissions.
evidence: dialogs.rs lines 133-137 returns PathBuf('python') unconditionally because that candidate is accepted without existence/provenance verification.
backend_process.rs lines 356-375 launches that result directly and sets only PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE/productized markers.
python_path_with_src_root preserves the entire inherited PYTHONPATH after the release src root.
No -I/-s/-P equivalent, PYTHONNOUSERSITE, cleared PYTHONHOME/PYTHONPATH policy, executable hash check, or release-only rejection was found.
The prereq script's import probe does not run inside start_backend and does not establish productized runtime provenance.
existing_safeguards: bundled runtime paths are tried before PATH
src root is prepended before inherited PYTHONPATH
health and route-contract checks run after spawn
safeguard_gap: Post-spawn functional checks cannot prove code provenance; a compatible shadow backend can satisfy them, and arbitrary import-time code runs before any check.
tests_missing: release-build rejection when bundled Python is absent
hostile PATH/PYTHONPATH/user-site shadow module tests
verified executable/package manifest test in installed layout
recommended_remediation: Make release builds require a manifest-verified bundled interpreter under the installed immutable root. Launch with a deliberately constructed environment and isolated import policy, clearing inherited Python variables/user site while adding only verified application paths. Retain PATH convenience only behind an explicit development mode.
remediation_risk: medium-high: Python isolation can break legitimate bundled native dependencies or runtime overlays; enumerate and test every required import/resource path rather than reopening broad inherited search paths
validation_rung: Rung 5 clean-machine package startup plus hostile PATH/PYTHONPATH/PYTHONHOME/user-site fixtures, runtime hash verification, backend contract suite, and package open/close; no real media required
prior_audit_relationship: New release provenance defect; prior runtime fallback tests prove ordering but not the trust boundary between developer and productized launches.

title: Backend stdout and stderr are read and logged as unbounded physical lines
observed_behavior: Both drain threads use BufRead::lines(), which allocates until a newline or EOF before any bound is applied. After bootstrap, stdout and all stderr lines are redacted but printed in full. Bootstrap context truncation therefore happens only after an arbitrarily large line was already allocated.
expected_invariant: Every child-process output path must enforce byte and line bounds while reading, before allocation and logging, so a faulty backend cannot exhaust shell memory or flood logs.
root_cause: Bounds are implemented as string preview/context helpers downstream of an unbounded line decoder, and the general drain paths have no output-size or rate cap.
failure_scenario: A backend bug or imported dependency writes a multi-gigabyte unterminated line, or emits very large newline-delimited payloads. The shell drain thread grows memory until exhaustion or writes unbounded diagnostic output, potentially terminating the UI while media work continues.
evidence: spawn_backend_stdout_reader lines 548-555 clones the complete String returned by reader.lines before sending or logging it.
spawn_pipe_drain lines 569-575 logs each complete stderr String without bounded_text.
The documented MAX_BOOTSTRAP_STDOUT bounds apply only in read_backend_bootstrap after line allocation.
Unit tests bound stored bootstrap context but do not exercise an oversized physical line or post-bootstrap output flood.
existing_safeguards: pipes are continuously drained to avoid deadlock
tokens are redacted
bootstrap context line count and rendered character length are bounded
safeguard_gap: Those controls act after unbounded allocation and do not cap ongoing drain output.
tests_missing: oversized unterminated stdout/stderr line
bounded chunk decoding across UTF-8 boundaries
post-bootstrap rate/volume limit
continued drain without memory growth
recommended_remediation: Replace lines() with a bounded incremental reader that caps retained bytes per logical line, discards or hashes overflow while continuing to drain, and rate-limits bounded log previews. Record truncation counters without exposing tokens.
remediation_risk: medium: the reader must not deadlock the child, split UTF-8 unsafely, hide the bootstrap record, or lose the first actionable diagnostics
validation_rung: Focused Rust adversarial pipe tests with multi-megabyte unterminated and flooding streams, bootstrap/health tests, and launch/close smoke; no real media required
prior_audit_relationship: New implementation-level gap in the documented bounded-output guardrail.

title: Backend HTTP calls have no total request deadline
observed_behavior: The helper sets two-second connect/read/write timeouts, then reads until EOF or the 16 MiB cap. A peer that returns at least one byte before each read timeout can keep the loop alive indefinitely because there is no wall-clock deadline or Content-Length/chunk framing completion rule.
expected_invariant: Startup, health, shutdown, and close-readiness requests must have bounded end-to-end duration independent of incremental peer progress, and lifecycle UI callbacks must remain responsive.
root_cause: Per-system-call socket timeouts are treated as a total HTTP deadline, while the manual HTTP/1.1 reader depends on Connection: close and has no elapsed-time budget.
failure_scenario: A wedged or compromised loopback backend dribbles one byte every 1.9 seconds. Startup validation, lifecycle monitoring, or the synchronous close-readiness path can block forever; the operator cannot safely close or recover through the native shell.
evidence: request_backend_json lines 33-35 configures only per-operation socket timeouts.
read_backend_response_capped lines 123-134 loops until read returns zero and never checks elapsed time.
The request asks for Connection: close and ignores response Content-Length/chunk termination.
request_close_readiness invokes this helper synchronously from the close-event decision path.
existing_safeguards: loopback-only URL validation
two-second connect/read/write timeout
16 MiB response cap
close-readiness fails closed on returned transport errors
safeguard_gap: A slow-progress response is neither an error nor oversized, so it bypasses every current bound.
tests_present: loopback URL and capped-response unit tests
tests_missing: slow-drip server exceeding a total deadline
valid Content-Length completion without waiting for EOF
partial headers/body and chunked framing
close callback responsiveness under a stalled peer
recommended_remediation: Use a maintained HTTP client with explicit connect and total request deadlines, or add a monotonic deadline enforced across resolution, write, headers, and body reads with correct framing. Keep the response cap and fail-closed close behavior.
remediation_risk: medium: overly short deadlines can create false crash/unsafe-close signals during local load; centralize policy and test bounded retries without multiplying total delay
validation_rung: Focused Rust loopback adversarial tests, lifecycle/close unit tests, PG-1 close smoke, and package open/close; no real media required
prior_audit_relationship: New transport-level availability finding; existing timeout tests cover idle calls, not progress that perpetually resets a per-read timeout.

title: Bearer-token initialization runs on every navigation without an origin guard
observed_behavior: Both windows inject the backend bearer token into a window global using an unconditional initialization script. Neither builder registers on_navigation, and the script checks no window.location. Tauri 2.11.3 documents that initialization scripts run on all top-level navigations and recommends an origin check; on Windows they are also added to subframes.
expected_invariant: The backend bearer token must be exposed only to the exact validated loopback origin/window context that needs it, and unexpected navigation must be denied before untrusted document code can read the token.
root_cause: URL validation is performed once before initial window construction, but token injection is attached to the WebView lifetime rather than scoped to that validated navigation/origin.
failure_scenario: A future link, redirect, compromised backend response, or unexpected navigation loads a non-backend document in an existing window. The initialization script runs before that document's scripts and publishes the live backend token; the document exfiltrates it and an external process uses it against the loopback API.
evidence: lib.rs injects the token for both main and pipeline-log WebViews and never checks window.location in the generated script.
Exact-source search found no on_navigation callback or navigation allowlist.
Local tauri-2.11.3 source documentation at webview_window.rs lines 904-915 states all top-level navigations and Windows subframe behavior and recommends guarding window.location.
Current WebView source has no external navigation path, limiting immediate reachability but not enforcing the invariant.
existing_safeguards: initial URLs are validated as explicit HTTP loopback
CSP restricts normal backend document behavior
Tauri remote capabilities are restricted to loopback URLs
current application links stay same-origin
safeguard_gap: CSP belongs to the loaded document and cannot stop the privileged initialization script from publishing the token into an unexpected document; no navigation-time check exists.
tests_missing: unexpected top-level navigation is rejected
redirect to a different origin receives no token
Windows subframe behavior
pipeline-log navigation confinement
recommended_remediation: Add a strict on_navigation allowlist bound to the exact backend origin and make the initialization script itself verify window.location before assigning any secret. Prefer a narrower authenticated bridge or per-window scoped credential if practical, and clear sensitive globals on lifecycle failure.
remediation_risk: medium: origin comparison must handle normalized localhost/127.0.0.1/IPv6 and the dynamic port without allowing sibling ports or breaking same-origin backend navigation
validation_rung: Focused Rust origin/URL tests plus native WebView navigation/redirect tests for both windows, token non-disclosure checks, and package open/close; no real media required
prior_audit_relationship: New defense-in-depth secret-boundary gap proven against the exact Tauri version; current no-external-link posture reduces but does not eliminate the defect.

title: The release updater is registered but never checks, downloads, or installs an update
observed_behavior: run() registers tauri-plugin-updater and does nothing else with it. No Rust UpdaterExt/check/download/install call, JavaScript updater client, updater invoke permission, prompt surface, or close-readiness-gated installation path exists anywhere under apps/desktop. CI still publishes signed updater JSON/signatures, and the operator runbook states that the app uses prompted updates and must check close readiness before applying one.
expected_invariant: A release claiming prompted signed updates must have an executable in-app update flow that verifies metadata/signatures, asks the operator, blocks on backend close-readiness, shuts down safely, applies the update, and reports failures/recovery.
root_cause: Artifact publication and plugin scaffolding were implemented without an application-side updater state machine or operator surface; plugin registration alone does not initiate an update.
failure_scenario: A private-beta release publishes latest-beta.json and a signed installer. Installed clients never check the channel and cannot prompt or apply it, so security/bugfix updates require undocumented manual reinstall; alternatively a future direct plugin call could bypass the runbook's close-readiness requirement because no gate exists.
evidence: lib.rs line 112 only builds/registers the updater plugin.
Fixed-string searches found no UpdaterExt, download_and_install, downloadAndInstall, @tauri-apps/plugin-updater, or updater permission usage in apps/desktop.
PRIVATE_BETA_INSTALL_UPDATE_RUNBOOK.md lines 135-140 requires signed channel updates and close-readiness gating.
The release workflow generates updater config/channel/signature artifacts, proving distribution-side scaffolding but not a consuming client.
existing_safeguards: CI generates signed updater artifacts and channel JSON
release verifier checks signatures/checksums
backend exposes strict close-readiness and shutdown routes
safeguard_gap: No code connects those artifacts and lifecycle routes into an actual update operation.
tests_missing: available/no-update checks
signature/download/install failure paths
operator prompt/cancel
unsafe close-readiness blocks update
safe shutdown then update/restart
beta/stable channel switching
recommended_remediation: Implement a backend-close-readiness-gated native updater controller and clear operator UI. Keep download/verification separate from installation, require explicit confirmation, request safe backend shutdown immediately before apply, and preserve recovery/rollback evidence. Add only the minimum capabilities needed by the chosen Rust- or WebView-owned surface.
remediation_risk: high: update installation can terminate active work or replace binaries; it must not bypass strict close-readiness, token boundaries, signing, channel policy, or AppData migration guarantees
validation_rung: Rung 5 signed local update server/channel fixtures, available/no-update/corrupt-signature/network-failure cases, unsafe/safe close gating, install/restart/rollback on a clean Windows account; representative real-media validation is required for any update test that crosses active-work shutdown
prior_audit_relationship: Current changelog describes updater scaffolding; this finding reconciles that scaffold with the stronger active operator runbook claim and confirms the consumer path is absent.

title: PG-2 automation fabricates exact media-validation evidence without checking the files or backend facts
observed_behavior: The debug script hard-codes ffmpeg/subtitle/audio/completed-output/sidecar/size/pending/diagnostics checks true and writes exact claims for remux/published, no pending publish, and ActiveJobs return_code=0. The harness validates neither SourceFile nor OutputFile existence/content, then treats finding the appended record as success. It fetches commands and close-readiness but does not reconcile them with the fabricated claims; Decision is an unrestricted caller string.
expected_invariant: A PG-2/representative-media record must derive every checked flag, exact evidence value, route/publish result, sidecar, pending-publish state, and completion fact from current backend-authored or filesystem evidence for the named paths; missing proof must remain missing/hold-review.
root_cause: The automation constructs the desired record from caller-provided paths and expected narrative instead of collecting/validating authoritative evidence before append, while the append endpoint records the attestation without being able to verify those asserted observations.
failure_scenario: An operator supplies nonexistent, failed, wrong, or stale source/output paths and optionally Decision=accepted. The harness appends a record claiming successful exact-path remux/publish and all validation checks, returns ok, and that false record is later used to close a real-media release gate.
evidence: debug_webview.rs lines 182-201 sets eight checks true and emits exact route/pending/ActiveJobs values without any preceding API read.
The PowerShell harness converts paths to full strings but never Test-Path/probes either media file.

Lines 364-399 wait only for a matching appended record, fetch unrelated command/readiness payloads, and emit ok without validating record warnings, evidence provenance, route, sidecar, pending state, or media metadata.
The default decision is hold_review, but the parameter accepts arbitrary text and the debug script forwards it unchanged.
existing_safeguards: debug-only Rust compilation gate
explicit isolated SampleValidationLog path
default hold_review decision
backend append route returns command evidence/warnings
safeguard_gap: Debug-only and hold-review defaults do not make invented factual evidence true, and the harness ignores the response warnings/current authoritative state.
tests_missing: nonexistent/mismatched paths must fail
exact backend route/completed/pending/sidecar/ActiveJobs evidence binding
stale output/run rejection
accepted decision prohibited until every required proof is current
representative media hash/metadata comparison
recommended_remediation: Replace hard-coded checks/evidence with a backend-generated, provenance-bound validation projection keyed to source/output/run IDs. The harness should verify file existence and immutable source hash, fetch current completed/pending/command/diagnostic evidence, reject contradictions or stale runs, and allow acceptance only through an explicit operator review step.
remediation_risk: high: evidence collection must remain read-only for source media, avoid promoting/publishing output, and distinguish expected review-only OCR/subtitle failures from false success
validation_rung: Rung 5 adversarial nonexistent/stale/mismatched fixtures, backend evidence-contract tests, WebView append smoke, and representative real-media validation with source/output hashes and manual playback where required
prior_audit_relationship: New validation-integrity defect in the current canonical PG-2 append harness; prior scaffold tests assert shape but not truth of the authored evidence.

title: Tauri harness cleanup can terminate an unrelated backend started concurrently
observed_behavior: Each harness snapshots all processes whose command line contains mediapipeline.desktop.local_api_main, then treats every later matching PID as its own backend. Finally blocks force-stop every PID in that delta. There is no parent-process, bootstrap URL/token-capture, start-time, nonce, or shell ownership binding before cleanup.
expected_invariant: A validation harness may stop only the exact process tree it started and positively identified; process-name or temporal-delta matching must never authorize termination of another operator/test backend.
root_cause: Global WMI process discovery is used as lifecycle ownership evidence. Baseline subtraction distinguishes old from new processes but cannot distinguish the harness child from any unrelated backend started after the baseline.
failure_scenario: Another user, scheduled test, developer command, or service starts a Local API backend while a Tauri harness is waiting. Its PID enters newBackendIds. On normal completion or any exception, the harness calls taskkill/Stop-Process on that unrelated backend tree, interrupting active work and potentially leaving incomplete state/output.
evidence: All five scripts compute newBackendIds solely as current matching PIDs not present in baselineBackendIds.
All five finally blocks iterate the entire delta and call Stop-ProcessIdTree.
Several harnesses select the first delta PID for URL/token/evidence, so even their observations can bind to the wrong backend.
No per-launch nonce or verified parent/descendant relation appears in the discovery or cleanup paths.
existing_safeguards: preexisting matching PIDs are excluded by the baseline
shell and WebView2 processes are separately tracked
cleanup waits for graceful exit before force-stop in normal paths
safeguard_gap: A concurrently started process is absent from the baseline and therefore indistinguishable from the harness child; graceful waiting does not prevent the finally block from force-killing it.
tests_missing: unrelated backend starts after baseline and survives success/failure cleanup
multiple new matching backends
PID reuse/start-time checks
verified process-tree ownership from launcher to backend
recommended_remediation: Have the launched shell/backend emit a per-run nonce and authenticated capture containing its exact PID/start time, or bind through a verified parent/Job Object relationship. Track only that identity and descendants, revalidate PID/start time before termination, and refuse ambiguous cleanup with actionable diagnostics.
remediation_risk: high: process ownership changes must still reliably clean the harness tree without weakening active-work close-readiness or killing shared tooling
validation_rung: Windows adversarial process tests with two concurrent backends, PID/start-time/parent spoof cases, every success/failure finally branch, PG-1/PG-2 harness smokes, and representative active-work protection; real-media validation is required before trusting cleanup around active work
prior_audit_relationship: New destructive harness-isolation defect found across five current canonical scripts.

title: A personal server name, user identity, and media paths are embedded in package-included Rust source
observed_behavior: A tracked Rust test hard-codes \\LAYNE-SERVER\Users\Layne\Videos source/output paths. The portable release exclusion policy returns included for this src/lib_tests path even when IncludeTests is false, while content-scan eligibility is false because scanning is limited to docs and pipeline config.
expected_invariant: Distributed source/packages must not disclose a developer's personal identity, internal host/share topology, or private media directory layout; test fixtures should use synthetic neutral paths and tests must be classified consistently.
root_cause: Rust tests live under the production src tree, outside both release test-exclusion patterns, and the source content is exempt from privacy scanning. A real operator path was used where a synthetic fixture would suffice.
failure_scenario: A portable release or source package is shared externally and includes lib_tests/mod.rs, disclosing the Layne identity, LAYNE-SERVER hostname, Users share layout, and internal Encode/outsource media organization.
evidence: lib_tests/mod.rs lines 775-776 contain the unredacted UNC paths.
Get-MediaPipelineReleaseExclusionReason returned <included> for apps/desktop/tauri/src-tauri/src/lib_tests/mod.rs with default release settings.
Test-MediaPipelineReleaseContentScanEligible returned false for the same path.
The assertion only needs Windows/UNC separator behavior and does not depend on real names or topology.
existing_safeguards: tests and ops/pipeline/tests directories are excluded by default
selected docs/config text is privacy-scanned
release manifest hashes included source
safeguard_gap: Nested Rust test modules are neither excluded nor scanned; hashing proves integrity, not privacy.
tests_present: release policy tests for selected personal config and test directories
tests_missing: Rust cfg(test)/lib_tests package exclusion or scan assertion
repository privacy scan for UNC host/user literals
neutral fixture requirement for source-embedded tests
recommended_remediation: Replace the literal with a synthetic UNC path and update release policy to exclude nested test-only Rust modules or make all included text source privacy-scan eligible with narrowly reviewed language-fixture allowances. Add a regression for this exact class.
remediation_risk: low: preserve UNC parsing/separator coverage while removing real identifiers; avoid excluding production Rust modules by a broad src pattern
validation_rung: Focused Rust unit test, release-policy tests, rebuilt portable package manifest/content scan, and inspection confirming the identifiers are absent; no real media required
prior_audit_relationship: Same package-boundary class as W13-001 but a distinct root cause and artifact: unredacted text under a nested Rust test module rather than a binary evidence screenshot.

title: The prerequisite check can report a non-MSVC link command as the MSVC linker
observed_behavior: Resolve-CommandPath returns the first PATH command named link before performing its Visual Studio-specific vswhere search. The result is labeled MSVC linker and any nonempty path satisfies -RequireBuildTools, without checking the file's Visual Studio location, PE version metadata, or ability to link an MSVC target. Git/MSYS commonly supplies an unrelated link.exe.
expected_invariant: A required MSVC build-tools check must verify the Visual Studio C++ workload, VsDevCmd environment, and the actual Microsoft linker/toolchain architecture rather than command-name coincidence.
root_cause: The generic PATH-first resolver is reused for a tool name whose identity is ambiguous, and the required gate reduces provenance to a Boolean path.
failure_scenario: Git usr/bin precedes Visual Studio tools on PATH. The script prints OK MSVC linker and exits successfully under -RequireBuildTools, but subsequent cargo/Tauri linking fails or invokes the wrong utility, invalidating clean-machine prerequisite evidence.
evidence: Resolve-CommandPath lines 28-31 returns any first command named link before lines 46-55 execute the constrained Visual Studio search.
Lines 151-162 label that path MSVC linker and make only its truthiness release-significant.
No VsDevCmd check or link.exe version/provenance invocation exists in this script.
Test-TauriShell-Build has a separate VsDevCmd requirement in its non-skip path, but that does not repair the standalone prereq report.
existing_safeguards: vswhere fallback constrains Visual Studio discovery
canonical build script also resolves VsDevCmd
actual cargo build eventually exposes a wrong linker
safeguard_gap: The advertised prerequisite gate can pass before either safeguard is exercised, and PG evidence can record that false pass.
tests_missing: fake/Git link.exe earlier on PATH must fail
valid VS linker via vswhere must pass
missing VsDevCmd/workload must fail RequireBuildTools
x64 host/target verification
recommended_remediation: For link, bypass the generic PATH-first result unless it is proven to belong to a qualifying Visual Studio installation. Resolve VsDevCmd/workload with vswhere, enter/query that environment, validate Microsoft link.exe provenance/version, and report each component separately.
remediation_risk: low-medium: Visual Studio editions and Build Tools layouts vary; use vswhere component queries rather than hard-coded edition paths
validation_rung: Focused PowerShell fixture tests for fake and valid linkers, clean developer-shell/pristine-shell runs, canonical Tauri build check, and PG-3 prerequisite evidence; no real media required
prior_audit_relationship: New false-positive prerequisite-gate defect; the canonical build's stronger separate VsDevCmd check previously masked it.

title: Canonical Tauri validation omits rustfmt while current Rust files fail cargo fmt --check
observed_behavior: cargo fmt --check exits 1 with diffs in backend_process/tests.rs and close_readiness.rs. The canonical Test-TauriShell-Build script runs npm check and cargo test --lib but no formatting check, so it passed while the formatter gate was red.
expected_invariant: The canonical Tauri validation surface must run the repository's required deterministic Rust formatting check and current checked-in Rust must pass it.
root_cause: Formatting is absent from the Tauri build wrapper and current edits were validated only by compilation/tests, allowing mechanical drift to persist.
failure_scenario: CI or a release gate that relies on Test-TauriShell-Build reports green, while a later rustfmt-enforcing check fails and blocks integration; repeated drift also obscures semantic diffs in lifecycle-critical tests.
evidence: cargo fmt --check was reproduced twice with the same import/wrapping diffs.
Test-TauriShell-Build lines 137-155 runs syntax, npm check, and cargo test only.
The same canonical build wrapper passed all 56 Rust tests despite the formatting failure.
existing_safeguards: Rust compilation and 56 unit tests pass
rustfmt is installed and independently runnable
safeguard_gap: No canonical wrapper or checked evidence binds rustfmt success to the green Tauri result.

title: Rust startup contract omits both priority-export routes
observed_behavior: REQUIRED_ROUTES includes queue priority/strategy/override routes but omits GET and POST /api/queue/priority-export. The authoritative Python Local API contract and inventory contain both. The exact scaffold reconciliation test fails with those two missing pairs while the canonical Rust/npm build remains green.
expected_invariant: The native startup compatibility gate must exactly cover the active backend route contract needed by the shipped WebView/release, including newly added read and mutation surfaces, so an incomplete or stale backend cannot be accepted.
root_cause: The Python route contract was extended without updating the manually duplicated Rust REQUIRED_ROUTES list, and the canonical Tauri wrapper does not run the cross-language scaffold reconciliation test.
failure_scenario: The shell starts against a stale backend that lacks priority export because health and the reduced Rust contract pass. The current WebView exposes export controls, but requests fail only when the operator uses them, after startup was declared compatible.
evidence: routes.rs queue GET lines 19-24 has no /api/queue/priority-export.
routes.rs queue POST lines 59-65 has no /api/queue/priority-export.
Python contract files expose both GET and POST routes and API_ROUTE_INVENTORY marks them active.
